why: Segment sales of $32-225 million for mountain, city and cargo e-bikes, with city bikes growing fastest and cargo bikes small but rising, are believable for a regional e-bike market.
Stations serving 350-1,000 customers a day with 4-7 minutes at the pump, a $2 million build cost and $5 profit per customer (fuel plus shop) give a payback of about 2.4 years, which is plausible.

A $6.8 billion coatings maker eyeing a $62 billion neighbouring market out of a $290 billion global total is within a factor of two of real figures, and a running-total curve that reaches exactly 100% across 50 provinces is consistent.

58,000 enquiries, a 57% conversion, 78% acceptance, 15% of a 260,000 declared value reclassified at a 4% duty rate and a half share of savings imply about $19 million in fees, a believable size for a customs-recovery firm.

Seed revenues of $180-410 million against markets of $1-2.4 billion (roughly 17-18% share) and 40-65 reps per crop give $3.5-7.5 million revenue per rep, high but within a few times of what a seed seller could report.
Lease fees of $510-590 a month on 7,100-9,300 cars, workshops billing $76-95 an hour for 1,500-2,400 hours a week, and margins of 3-6% for leasing and 16-18% for workshops are all realistic.
Twelve desks with $2-22 million in fees and 9-78 consultants each give about $105 million from 414 consultants, roughly $130-350 thousand per consultant, which matches real recruitment billing.
Products with $1-38 million revenue and 9-65 developers give about $117 million from 325 developers, around $360 thousand per developer, a believable figure for a small-business software firm.
Loyalty members spending $21-75 per half-year at a bookshop, with falls of 18-45% as e-readers spread, are plausible even though quintile 3 spends a little less than quintile 2.
Burger restaurants serving 650-2,100 customers a day with 3-8 minutes from order to food, a $1.2 million build cost and $1 profit per customer are in line with busy fast-food outlets.
